```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2movies)

source()
```


## Summary statistics

In the following table, basic statistics for the relevant numerical
variables in the dataset are summarised

```{r}
movies %>% 
  select(2:6) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = "variable", 
               values_to ="value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Minimum = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing = sum(is.na(value))) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_number(columns = c(Mean, Minimum, Maximum, Missing),
             decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Movies - Summary statistics"
  )
```

## Visualize data distributions

The distribution of each relevant numerical variable can be visualized
in the following density graphs. These are: year, length, budget,
rating, and number of votes.

```{r}

movies %>% 
  pivot_longer(
  cols = 2:6,   
  names_to = "variable",      
  values_to = "value"         
) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = variable, colour = variable)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ variable, 
    scales = "free",
  labeller = as_labeller(c(
    "year" = "Year",
    "length"= "Length",
    "budget"= "Budget",
    "rating"= "Rating",
    "votes"= "Number of votes"))) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Visualize rating patterns

We consider the 100 movies with the highest average rating and plot in a
heatmap the percentage of votes awarding 1-10 ratings. This will
visualize whether these top-rated movies have similar distribution
between rating points.

```{r}
library(superheat)

heatmap_rating <- 
  clean_movies %>% 
  select(title, rating, r1:r10) %>% 
  arrange(desc(rating)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
  {
    matrix_rating <- as.matrix(select(., r1:r10))
    rownames(matrix_rating) <- .$title
    superheat(
      matrix_rating,
      pretty.order.rows = FALSE,        
      yr = .$rating,                  
      yr.plot.type = "bar",
      yr.axis.name = "Average Rating",
      yr.bar.col = "lightblue4",
      heat.col.scheme = "viridis",
      grid.hline.col = "white",
      grid.vline.col = "white",
      left.label.text.size = 2.5,
      bottom.label.text.angle = 0
    )
  }
```


#### Impact of 10/10 votes on average rating

We also investigate whether the percentage of users who awarded a 10/10
rating (r10 variable) can predict the average rating of a movie.

```{r}
fit_r10 <- 
  lm(rating ~ 1 + r10, 
     data = clean_movies) 

summary(fit_r10)

# Visualise diagnostic plots of the linear model in one figure
plot_lm_r10 <- fit_r10 %>% 
  {par(mfrow = c(2, 2));
    plot(.)}
# no clear violations of the requirements
```

The low p-value and adjusted R\^2 of 0.1789 reveal a correlation,
although weak, between r10 and rating. This can be visualized on the
following scatter plot of the r10 data.

```{r}
r10_rating_plot <- ggplot(
  clean_movies, 
      aes(r10, rating)) +
      geom_point() +
  labs(dictionary = c(
    rating = "Average rating /10",
    r10 = "Percentage of 10/10 votes")) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", 
              formula = y ~ 1 + x, 
              se = FALSE, 
              color = "red3", 
              linetype = 1)

print(r10_rating_plot)
```
